name: Aimtron Electronics Limited
sector: Electronics design and manufacturing; PCB assembly and box-build
summary: Aimtron is a rapidly expanding electronics design and manufacturing business, with Indian PCB assembly/box-build operations and a newly acquired US manufacturing business. Parent revenue expansion is genuine in the reported history, and the US operation and new qualifications offer identifiable growth avenues. However, growth has consumed substantial cash. Material consolidated loan/elimination questions, ambiguous statutory-account labels, and an unquantified contingent acquisition payment prevent a dependable group capital-return and shareholder-return model. At the verified 19 October close of ₹1,701.40, the issued equity value is ₹3,649.89 crore, about 79.4 times reported FY26 group earnings. This is a growth/integration thesis on research hold, not an evidence-backed compounder or an actionable low-price opportunity. A reconciled group opening balance sheet, acquisition funding/consideration bridge and cash collections would change the assessment more than another order announcement. [S1,S6,S7,S10,S15]
identity_note: Official NSE/issuer filings match ISIN; actual September allotments override stale security-master capital.
score_note: Completed evidence-led review with specific unresolved group ledgers and acquisition obligations. Numeric factors retained only where supported; aggregates NS, not a midpoint or a low score for missingness.

gates.reason: Connected commercial balances and material transparency weaknesses; no established diversion or intentional fraud in reviewed evidence.
Material consolidation/elimination and statutory-account classification questions prevent a certified group capital/earnings/funding bridge.
Actual equity receipts exist, but available cash, facilities and full acquisition claims remain unresolved. No observed default conclusion.
Observed turnover supports small-position theoretical capacity, but LTASM-I and lot granularity require execution checks.

GOV.reason: Material transparency weaknesses and connected working-capital exposure. Actual issuance and the unmodified audit are contrary evidence; no proven abuse or governance override.

MOAT.reason: Engineering and qualification relationships exist, but the pilot remains conditional. Historical concentration and competing qualified EMS suppliers limit demonstrated durability.

REV.reason: Parent five-year growth37.26% and alternative three-year growth45.48–53.15% support the ≥30% band. Starting9 is capped at8 for Medium comparability; no single-quarter bonus or acquired-group shortcut.

DUR.reason: Acquired capacity and Indian integration provide actual access. Commissioning, customer qualification, order cancellation and funding constrain the runway.

CAP.reason: Full acquisition capital, elimination and ambiguous balance classifications prevent reliable incremental ROIC; forecast returns are not historical evidence.

CASH.reason: Persistent negative paired reported CFO versus substantial PAT, large WIP/receivables and supplier advances. Actual equity helps finance growth but does not repair cash conversion.

BAL.reason: Actual capital raises and reported debt are known; earnout, external versus intercompany claims, facilities and cash availability are insufficiently bounded to certify survival.

EXEC.reason: Completed acquisition and parent growth are positive. Cash integration and greenfield qualification remain unproved; not all guidance is assumed missed.

EARN.reason: Operating profit growth is reported, but inventory valuation and group elimination/audit-scope questions prevent certifying normalized per-share profit quality.

R.reason: No supported full group cash/debt/dilution/earnout bridge. Parent-only enterprise value cannot produce an investable IRR.

D.reason: Parent linked stress quantifies needs, but unbounded group claims and unknown subsidiary value preclude a certified shareholder-recovery band.

P.reason: As-reported multiples and reverse algebra are visible, but unsupported group margins and financing prevent a fully supported price-expectations factor.

L.reason: Starting 9 for no more than two theoretical exit days; deduct 1 for verified LTASM/restriction risk and 1 for lot granularity/unverified spread. One 200-share lot costs ₹340,280; two cost ₹680,560, exceeding the ₹5 lakh reference.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Missing material factors and unresolved G2. Known-score bounds are not point rankings.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Aimtron is a rapidly expanding electronics design and manufacturing business, with Indian PCB assembly/box-build operations and a newly acquired US manufacturing business. At the verified 19 October close of ₹1,701.40, the issued equity value is ₹3,649.89 crore, about 79.4 times reported FY26 group earnings. This is a growth/integration thesis on research hold, not an evidence-backed compounder or an actionable low-price opportunity. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Aimtron Electronics Limited, NSE SME AIMTRON, ISIN INE0RUV01018. Cutoff: 20 October 2026 UTC. Quote: official NSE close on 19 October 2026, not a live executable offer. Actual issued shares: 21,452,279 after the September conversion, not the stale April count in the security master. Five-year analytical horizon; 15% nominal equity hurdle before investor taxes; illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, not a suggested allocation. INR crore unless stated. [S6,S7,S15]

Preferred scope is consolidated, but it cannot presently support a certified investment model. Audited parent accounts and an explicitly isolated parent operating/funding diagnostic are retained alongside the group disclosures. The financial policies state Indian GAAP Accounting Standards and AS 3; the audit report also uses Ind AS wording. The exchange structured filing is explicitly NONINDAS. That conflict is not resolved by assuming every listed issuer uses Ind AS. [S1,S20]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. Commercial related-party activity and disclosure weaknesses require scrutiny, but the reviewed evidence does not establish diversion or deliberate fraud. G2 Reliability: Hold — unresolved. This is not merely a semantic subsidiary description: the group retains a ₹16.8011 crore loan identified as to its wholly owned US subsidiary; ₹37.9289 crore appears as an asset under a liability label; a separate ₹33.0335 crore statutory-liability balance has no usable ledger breakdown. The amounts and classifications materially affect capital, funding and recoverable value. G3 Funding: Conditional, not a finding of current default. Actual equity receipts help, but do not establish unspent, fungible funds or the full acquisition obligation. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Turnover supports a small reference-position exit estimate, but lot granularity and verified LTASM-I restrictions matter. [S1,S7,S11,S15–S18]

Confidence is Medium on retrieved parent revenue, historical reported cash weakness, actual allotments and dated turnover; Low on consolidated eliminations, economic capital returns and complete acquisition liabilities. Forecast uncertainty is independently high. The weakest material area makes the overall investment conclusion Low confidence. [S1–S20]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 4; MOAT 5; REV 8; DUR 6; CAP NS; CASH 2; BAL NS; EXEC 5; EARN NS. These are not nine separate penalties for the same disclosure issue. CASH measures observed cash realization; GOV reflects transparency and stewardship; CAP/BAL/EARN remain unavailable where the unresolved scope directly affects their evidence. [E1–E12]

BQS known contribution = 0.20×4 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.10×2 + 0.08×5 = 3.96. Coverage 80%; mathematical missing-data bound 4.16–5.96. Final BQS NS. GQS known contribution = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.10×2 = 4.60. Coverage 70%; uncapped bound 4.90–7.60. Persistent poor cash conversion would cap a completed GQS at 5, but cannot turn an incomplete score into 5. Final GQS NS. IAS: R/D/P NS; L 7, Medium confidence; BQS is unavailable, so IAS NS. None of the aggregates is ranking-eligible. G2 also independently prevents a favorable investment classification. Moving the two uncertain scored factors GOV/MOAT by one point changes known BQS by ±0.40; it does not cure missing CAP/BAL. [E1–E12]

REV uses the parent, not acquired group revenue: reported FY21-to-FY26 endpoints imply 37.26% CAGR. The alternative original/restated FY23 parent bases imply 45.48%–53.15% three-year growth; both exceed the same ≥30% rubric threshold. Starting 9 is capped to 8 for Medium confidence/comparability limitations, with no extra trajectory bonus for one quarter. This is demonstrated parent-reported expansion, not a claim that all group growth is organic. [S1–S4,E3]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The listed company supplies PCB assemblies, engineering/design services and increasingly integrated box-build products. Qualification, component sourcing, testing, traceability and timely delivery matter to industrial, power, communications, medical and rugged-electronics customers. Components are procured and substantial work-in-progress can precede shipment and payment; revenue growth is therefore not equivalent to cash generation. Customer purchase orders can change or be cancelled, and the prospectus describes limited protection for surplus components. [S1,S4]

The owned group must be separated from similarly branded private promoter-group companies. Aimtron Electronics LLC is the US wholly owned subsidiary; Aimtron International Controls LLC is its step-down business, operating the acquired ICS assets from February 2026. Aimtron Mechatronics is the Indian subsidiary developing additional capabilities. Aimtron Corporation and several other US/Indian related parties are not interchangeable with this listed ownership perimeter. Group-wide employee/customer marketing claims should not automatically be attributed to listed shareholders. [S1,S5,S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism: engineering participation, customer qualification and reliable low-volume/high-mix production can create switching friction. Evidence includes existing manufacturing operations, repeat programmes and new pilot engagements. Durability depends on consistent quality, design relevance and successful customer qualification, not a famous customer logo. Failure modes include competing qualified EMS vendors, component obsolescence, customer redesigns and cancelled orders. The September Curtiss-Wright announcement explicitly describes a pilot subject to qualification and future requirements, not a guaranteed production programme. No verified market-share denominator or demonstrated broad pricing monopoly was found. MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable capabilities. [S1,S4,S9]

Economically relevant comparators illustrate both sides. Cyient DLM's FY26 issuer release reports revenue ₹1,261.5 crore, down 17%, and normalized EBITDA margin 10.3%, showing that qualification-heavy work does not eliminate demand cycles. Syrma's FY26 operating revenue was ₹4,819.1 crore, up 27.2%, with operating EBITDA margin 11.3% and operating cash ₹289.6 crore; its larger consumer/auto mix makes it an imperfect margin comparator. Kaynes' FY26 group revenue was ₹3,626.354 crore, while CFO was negative ₹600.404 crore; its metering, acquisition and semiconductor exposures make the cause different, not an excuse for Aimtron. These are economic context, not a precise market-multiple peer ranking or an assertion of superior governance. [S21–S23]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Historical reported revenue/PAT/CFO/cash capex:
- FY21 restated parent: 52.7793 / 15.7172 / 6.2219 / 0.6954.
- FY22 restated parent: 26.3192 / −1.8015 / 8.6205 / 21.9869.
- FY23 restated parent: 71.5836 / 8.6319 / −10.9196 / 1.8151.
- FY24 later comparative, before subsidiaries: 92.9759 / 13.5994 / 6.6898 / 3.9715.
- FY25 group: 159.1838 / 25.6309 / −18.6716 / 12.9593.
- FY26 group: 301.1592 / 45.9730 / −39.9593 / 47.4760. [S1–S4]

These rows are not a silently spliced organic series. The FY24 annual's original FY23 comparator is revenue 83.5062 / PAT 12.0004, whereas the IPO restatement gives 71.5836 / 8.6319. The ₹4.0694 crore cumulative equity restatement is explicitly charged to FY24 reserves; the exact revenue reclassification is not located. FY24 original CFO 6.7091 differs from the later 6.6898, and its financing cash flow includes a noncash restatement adjustment. Ten-year CAGR is ND. Group annual additions were66.2079 and141.9754 in FY25/FY26, but include perimeter changes. Parent revenue rose from 158.3073 to 257.1341 in FY26, an addition 98.8268, about 62.43%; this supports strong growth without counting all US-acquired sales as organic. [S1–S4]

The July business update reports Q1 FY27 group sales 84.01 versus 43.30, and backlog 604 as of June 30. These are management business-update figures, not a complete audited quarter with cash flow. No TTM profit/CFO is manufactured. The acquisition contributed only about USD 1.6m for two FY26 months according to the April call; the AOC-1 foreign reporting-period label does not provide a clean acquisition/organic bridge. [S10,S12]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible avenues include Indian box-build/mechanical integration, expanded SMT capacity, acquired US industrial customers and qualified new programmes. The January acquisition presentation describes four SMT lines, roughly 54–55% starting utilization, and a phased ambition near 90% over three years. It estimates incremental US capex 5–6 and working capital 5–6 crore. These are management estimates, not already financed capacity. The Indian greenfield development has a stated 100-crore plan; April commentary puts mechanical readiness around late FY27 and electronics thereafter. The relevant test is commissioned, qualified and cash-generating output, not an announced plant. [S1,S5,S10]

Management's FY27 revenue 450–550 and longer-term 40–50% CAGR are not the base case by default. The existing balance sheet already carries inventory 103.1758 and receivables 135.4709 at group level, and the cash absorption does not disappear merely because demand exists. Acquired ICS's starting EBITDA margin was about 11%, not the 20–22% group aspiration. No return on all acquisition consideration can be certified without the price, earnout and elimination bridge. CAP remains NS rather than a reassuring peer average. GQS remains incomplete, with a cash-conversion cap applicable if the other factors become scoreable. [S1,S5,S10]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
FY26 disclosed related-party dealings include sales 9.3167 and purchases 12.5804 with Aimtron Corporation; advances against purchases 20.1696 and closing debit 25.1832 to that company are material against cash. Other related parties also receive services/advances. These are disclosed commercial transactions, not proof of abuse. The central questions are pricing, ageing, settlement and whether the listed company bears working-capital risk for the wider private group. Historical IPO concentration was substantial: top 10 customers 96.70% in FY23 and largest group customer 55.99%; current comparable top-customer concentration is ND, while actual Corporation sales have fallen materially as a share of reported group revenue. [S1,S4]

The audit opinion is unmodified, but KAMs discuss an undeveloped slow/nonmoving-inventory policy, scrap policy, asset tagging, a bankrupt overseas customer's write-off, evolving foreign-currency consolidation policy and a conditional seller payment. These are specific control/reporting matters, not a fraud finding. The same annual audit page describes reliance on other auditors and also parent-approved unaudited overseas statements. The April results do not resolve that later wording conflict. Auditor firm restructuring involved the same partners and an LLP reorganization; it is not evidence of a resignation over withheld information. [S1,S2,S20]

The prospectus disclosed historical FEMA reporting delays and prospective compounding/late fees. FY26 secretarial audit reports compliance for its reviewed period; no specific closure order for every historical item was located, so continuing noncompliance is not asserted. The FY26 notes disclose a 7.9081-crore tax contingency and deposit 0.7908129, not a final adverse outcome. A prior GST-demand line disappearing is not independently verified litigation resolution. [S1,S4]

Promises versus delivery: the IPO funding-use filing reports all 87.02 used; the FY26 warrant statement separately says 33.61 received and 19.26 used. January acquisition completion is evidenced by operations from February and subsequent sales/bookings. September US bookings USD 11.8m and five customer additions are new orders, not collected revenue. The greenfield timing and pilot qualification remain milestones to verify. EXEC5 reflects demonstrated scaling alongside unresolved cash/integration execution. [S5,S9–S14]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY24–FY26 paired reported group CFO sums to−51.9411 versus PAT85.2033, a ratio−0.610. The associated reported capex totals64.4068, making the reported FCF proxy−116.3479 before acquisition/other investment flows. Scope changes and historical CF presentation mean this is not an economic FCFF certification; nevertheless, the evidence does not support strong operating cash realization. Capex is not the explanation for negative CFO. [S1–S4]

FY26 reported group PBT60.9082 includes other income2.3551, finance cost0.6842 and depreciation6.5372. An operating EBIT calculation excluding other income and the tiny0.004 exceptional gain is59.2333, and EBITDA65.7705, but both depend on inventory and consolidation reliability. Work-in-progress rose from 11.6205 to 79.2787; inventory-change credit 67.6629 exceeds reported PBT. Inventory capitalization is normal accrual accounting in principle, not proof of fabricated earnings, but realizability is decisive given the audit policy gaps and the earlier 4.7562 inventory restatement. EARN is therefore NS, not automatically1. [S1,S4]

Reported group borrowings 54.8177 long-term plus 0.4906 short-term omit bank CC 22.3923 classified inside other current liabilities. Including those and credit cards 0.0157 gives 77.7163 of reported debt-like balances, not proof that every group related-party balance is external after elimination. Parent reported funded debt is 22.8986 on the same classification. The group cash-flow closing 11.8759 versus balance-sheet 13.8759 reconciles to a 2-crore deposit exceeding three months; this is not missing cash. April's structured cash flow included an extra 2-crore financing inflow, superseded by the annual presentation. [S1,S20]

Parent CFO −1.8426 is flattered by the 22.3923 CC increase inside operating liabilities. Reclassifying that funding gives −24.2349. Supplier advances rose 22.5780 and are substantially carried through investing loans/advances; adding that deployment yields −46.8129 before unresolved tax/noncash adjustments. This is a transparent classification sensitivity, not a certified normalized CFO. The forecast never subtracts those historical movements again. [S1]

Receivables older than six months in FY26 group ageing include 17.4887 at 6–12 months,0.1818 at 1–2 years and0.0118 disputed beyond 3 years. Not-due balances 77.0119 do not eliminate the collection burden. Trade payables 50.3831 contain substantial due balances; the existence of creditor support is not proof of durable negative working capital. [S1]

The diagnostic parent opening operating WC 177.3508 is rebuilt from actual AR 117.4218, inventory 80.2813, supplier advances 26.5249 and specified operating assets, less AP 42.6949, customer advances 4.3203, employee payables 1.3417 and expense provision 0.4919. Opening tax 12.85 and credits 9.2939 are excluded from WC and settled once as net 3.5561 if usable; gross-tax sensitivity pays 12.85. Ambiguous statutory asset 37.9289 and claim 33.0335 are separately tracked, never blindly netted. Subsidiary loans 24.6367 and investment 8.1826 are not liquid operating cash. Gratuity 0.0834 remains a terminal claim unless paid. No arbitrary opening liquidation of ordinary recurring payables is imposed. [S1,A1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Actual March shares 20,609,177 plus April 232,180, August 433,122 and September 177,800 equal 21,452,279. Post-March conversion cash is 43.038670896 at 75% of the680.64 warrant price, not the full issue price again. Remaining 350,934 old warrants could bring 17.914478832 by 2 March 2027. The proposed 1,224,265 shares at 1674.47 would raise 204.9995, but the October 22 EGM is after the cutoff. The authorized 200,000 ESOP pool is not the same as actual granted/vested options; minimum possible exercise price is 10. Current issued market cap 3649.8907 uses actual shares. Reported group P/E 79.39 and parent-only P/E 93.20 are scope-labeled cross-checks, not fair values. [S1,S6–S8,S13,S15]

The annual diagnostic is deliberately isolated parent operations, not an unsupported group SOTP. Bear/base/bull revenue paths end 272.64 / 680.42 / 981.51; operating margins 12→15% / 18% / 20%; capex 6% / 8% / 10% of revenue; operating tax 25.17%; existing-debt cash interest 10%. It assumes no new loan, no subsidiary distributions or recovery, no additional subsidy, and does not treat the proposed equity as completed. Actual opening operating WC is retained; the bear case does not release inventory automatically when sales fall. These assumptions test funding sensitivity, not proven capacity economics. [A1]

Before any opening free cash or equity application, cumulative peak needs are 0 / 108.20 / 235.49. Settling the separately labeled 33.0335 claim in year 1 instead of retaining it as a senior terminal claim changes them to 30.67 / 141.23 / 268.52. Denying opening tax-credit usability gives 6.93 / 117.50 / 244.78. These are alternative ledger/settlement treatments, not assertions that all ambiguous items are actual cash dues. Full recovery of the labeled asset is a separate optimistic sensitivity, never the reference. An additional 10-crore acquisition payment is an illustrative sensitivity, not a disclosed amount or a bound. [A1]

Reported parent cash 8.647 is shown separately, not called zero in the bank. The warrant-use statement's residual 33.61 − 19.26 = 14.35 requires tracing before any balance is called unrestricted. Actual post-March equity receipt does not prove it remains unspent or fungible for this isolated model. The reference holds existing facilities outstanding as an assumption, not verified rollover. A 50% parent-debt withdrawal paid once changes peak needs to 9.08 / 115.07 / 242.36 and reduces subsequent interest and terminal debt. The diagnostic's terminal parent EVs 367.23 / 1649.66 / 3525.44 use 12 / 18 / 24 times terminal NOPAT; they are mechanical components, not the value of all listed shares. No terminal price or investable IRR is issued. R/D/P and IAS remain NS because a full group equity bridge is unsupported. [S11,A1]

A separate reverse-expectations algebra illustrates the burden: at 25× terminal earnings, 15% net margin, no dividends and 23,227,478 hypothetical shares including all old warrants, proposed equity and maximum ESOP pool, a 15% five-year return requires PAT 317.95 and revenue 2119.66, or 47.74% annual growth from reported FY26 group sales. A 20 / 25 / 30× by 12 / 15 / 18% grid is retained in the diagnostic. This is not a funded forecast; further dilution and interest costs can make it harder. At 12%, 15% and 18% hurdles, the same 25×/15%-margin algebra requires revenue 1857.24 / 2119.66 / 2410.94, equivalent to 43.88% / 47.74% / 51.59% growth. A conditional entry-price range would imply false precision until the full model is resolved. [A1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not simply a lower multiple: cancelled/delayed programmes leave work-in-progress and supplier advances tied up; weaker collections and inventory recoverability force more financing; lower acquired margins and additional seller/project commitments consume the capital raise; new equity then dilutes per-share economics. Reliance on a private-group procurement/customer network adds counterparty exposure. Reported cash is small relative to these moving parts. The diagnostic illustrates funding sensitivity but cannot establish ultimate shareholder recovery without the consolidated ledger and acquisition contract. Impairment risk is High as an assessment of uncertainty and financing/valuation exposure, not a claim of an observed default. [S1,S4,S5,A1]

The strongest contrary evidence is substantial reported parent growth, new customer qualifications, actual completed equity receipts, acquired capacity and the unmodified opinion. Those positives justify completing the research rather than alleging misconduct; they do not settle the disputed scope. The single thesis-break variable is conversion of accumulated inventory/receivables into collectible, funded business without repeated adverse dilution. [S1,S6,S9,S12]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At today's price and the hypothetical 23,227,478 expanded shares, 5× and10× prices imply equity values about19760 and39519 crore. At 25× earnings and 15% net margin, that requires revenue about 5269 and 10538 crore, before further dilution or a less generous exit multiple. Those scales cannot be established merely by management's 1000-crore aspiration or a global EMS TAM. The accessible capacity, funding and group economics are not yet sufficient to support either outcome. Classification: speculative / unsupported, not an assigned probability. [A1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Group elimination and statutory-ledger reconciliation: baseline 16.8011 intercompany loan and 37.9289 / 33.0335 labeled balances. Obtain signed reconciliation before certifying capital or net claims; a material unexplained change is an investigation trigger.
2. Cash conversion: FY26 group CFO −39.9593 and parent −1.8426 before classification corrections. Require disclosed collections and a financing-separated cash bridge; further inventory growth without shipments/receipts weakens the thesis.
3. WIP and ageing: group WIP 79.2787, AR 135.4709. Track subsequent shipment, write-down and over-six-month migration, not just total sales.
4. Acquisition: obtain total paid/deferred/contingent consideration, external debt terms and subsidiary audited periods. No zero earnout assumption until resolved.
5. Warrant/new issue: remaining 350,934 warrants and proposed 1,224,265 equity. Verify actual exercise/allotment, cash receipt and use; shareholder authorization alone is not funding.
6. Greenfield: management's late FY27 mechanical readiness and subsequent electronics commissioning. Verify physical completion, customer qualification and actual capital spent; repeated delay without a funding revision is a warning.
7. Orders: June 30 backlog 604, September US bookingsUSD11.8m, pilot programmes. Reconcile execution/cancellations and cash terms rather than summing bookings twice.
8. Tradability: October 20 LTASM-I, lot 200, quoted close 1701.4. Recheck restrictions and depth before any implementation; historical average turnover does not promise exit. [S1,S5–S18]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved financial reliability; research priority is the balance-sheet and acquisition bridge. No favorable investment classification, aggregate ranking, buy/sell instruction or compounder designation is supported. The parent business shows meaningful expansion, but the current evidence cannot certify value creation per share for the entire group. A cheaper price alone would not resolve G2. The cash-conversion weakness remains relevant even if accounting presentation is subsequently reconciled. [E1–E12]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Source and evidence ledgers accompany this dossier. Principal unresolved items are the statutory-ledger identities and recoverability/timing; consolidated elimination of the US loan; actual foreign reporting/audit scope; total acquisition consideration and contingent payment; current available facilities and cash earmarks; comparable organic growth; exact old revenue restatement bridge; and actual ESOP grants. No official credit-rating rationale was located in the targeted issuer/agency search, so an aggregator's claimed rating is not adopted. [S1–S23]

The parent-only diagnostic is reproducible, uses actual opening claims, and leaves unsupported equity returns blank. Its ledger alternatives are not equivalent-probability scenarios or confidence intervals. Forward capex/WC/margins and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions, not management commitments. Historical source corrections and model uncertainty are kept distinct from issuer misconduct. No invented missing-factor midpoint, rescue facility, permanent tax rollover or subsidiary-loan double recovery is used. [A1]

valuation.status: parent-only operating/funding diagnostic, not a full investable equity model
valuation.forecast_period: FY2027–FY2031; FY27 includes elapsed months, not a claim of known October cash
valuation.opening_cash_treatment: Zero free cash assumed in diagnostic, not a claim the bank balance is zero. Reported cash is a separate potential funding source, subject to warrant proceeds earmarking. Never both added to cash and credited against funding need.
valuation.funding_qualification: Received money is not proof it remains unspent or available for these isolated parent uses. Compare needs with these ceilings, but do not certify funding. Proposed October22 authorization is after cutoff.
model_policy: Operating WC starts from actual disclosed balances, not a backward forecast ratio. Forecast proportional stocks are analyst sensitivities, not company guidance.
Recurring employee/expense operating claims are included both at opening and forecast closing; no arbitrary opening liquidation charge.
Tax asset and liability excluded from WC; net tax paid once, gross-tax sensitivity separate.

Ambiguous statutory asset excluded from all reference recovery; labeled liability retained as a separate senior terminal claim, or paid once in gross-settlement sensitivity. Neither is called a verified net claim.
No subsidiary-loan or equity recovery is assumed alongside subsidiary value. Group valuation is intentionally absent.
Gratuity .0834 remains terminal claim unless separately settled. Interest10% on existing parent reported funded debt; no new-debt availability or interest-tax shield assumed.

Reference holds existing parent facilities outstanding at10% illustrative cash interest, not a verified rollover commitment. Separate half-withdrawal stress repays once and reduces subsequent interest/terminal debt.
Capex6–10% of revenue tests capital-intensive scaling rather than treating depreciation as sufficient maintenance. No assertion that this expenditure buys a certified capacity quantity.
Bear declining sales do not release opening working capital mechanically. New provisions/credit losses are not claimed as historical facts.
Unquantified earnout sensitivities are NOT an upper bound or a claim that parent owes exactly10crore.
EV is an assumed exit multiple of parent NOPAT, not a full company fair value. R, group D and equity-price return remain NS.
